visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md. The KB-era index.html that used to sit in this directory was DELETED 2026-08-27: it was retired as a visual target on 2026-08-26 and kept only because ci:mockup-coverage required a parity.json beside any index.html, which is a gate keeping a dead file alive. The target is the patterns in PUBLIC_UI.md, built from components/site/v3. THIS FILE STILL BINDS: requiredComponents is what stops a page silently losing a section, and ci:mockup-parity reads it with or without a mockup.
competitiveTarget: Long-tail SEO: 'homes for sale in {zip}'. A ZIP is the CITY grain in PUBLIC_UI.md §3: the Field of this ZIP's houses opens the page, the verdict is a caption inside the market section, and child neighborhoods are doors below the fold.
note: MIGRATED TO THE v3 BARREL 2026-08-26. Four patterns, which is the rhythm cap: Field (the houses and their map) · Instrument (the market, and once per other property type the ZIP holds) · Ledger (the neighborhoods here, then the rest of the service area) · Sheet (listing alerts, then the seller door). No two adjacent sections share a pattern. The property-type run is ONE logical section under the 2026-08-26 enumeration amendment. THE PAGE CONTRACT is unchanged: same generateMetadata strings on both branches, same ten canonical ZIPs in the same order, dynamicParams=false, revalidate 60, the same three JSON-LD payloads with the same five Dataset variables, the section tracker, and the listing-alert capture payload. THE READS ARE UNCHANGED: one getZipListings call feeds the Field, its map and the neighborhood Ledger; getMetric (geoType 'zip', segment 'detached') overlays Market Truth on a hit; getPublicPlaceSegments / getPublicDetachedPace / getPublicDetachedMix / getPublicDetachedMonthly carry the leftover figures and the median-close overlay. MetadataBlock stays on the legacy register because ci:ai-structured-data pins this route to it by name and JSON-LD is not visual language.

requiredComponents.name: V3Chrome
requiredComponents.section: chrome — the public header, mounted by app/layout.tsx. Not a page-level import; ci:mockup-parity auto-satisfies this entry because the layout owns the header.

requiredComponents.name: V3SectionTracker
requiredComponents.section: tracking — section view + scroll depth. It derives pageType from the path, and lib/analytics/page-type.ts maps /zip/ to 'zip', so the emitted pageType is the same string the KB tracker sent.

requiredComponents.name: MetadataBlock
requiredComponents.section: AI-citability — BreadcrumbList + Place + Dataset JSON-LD, the same three payloads the KB page emitted. ci:ai-structured-data pins this route to MetadataBlock by name.

requiredComponents.name: V3Breadcrumb
requiredComponents.section: breadcrumb — Home > Homes for sale > {zip}. Surface tone, below-nav offset on.

requiredComponents.name: ZipHomesField
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 2, Field, route-local. Every active single-family listing that reports a list price, as a list of photographed rows bound both ways to the real Google map in the frame's map slot (PlaceFieldMap). The count is a caption naming the ZIP, never a number hero. Replaces KbHero, KbFeatured and KbListingMap: the ZIP's houses open the page instead of a stock regional photograph, and the list is the whole set rather than the top 14.

requiredComponents.name: V3Instrument
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 1, Instrument, level 1 — the market. The verdict is the caption sentence under the headline, the KPI row is the figure set (leftover HUD tiles, then the 12-month pace items the HUD does not already print, then the detached mix), and the median-close year overlay is the chart. Replaces KbMarketHud, PublicPaceStats and PublicMixStats.

requiredComponents.name: V3Ledger
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 3, Ledger, twice: the neighborhoods inside this ZIP with their count and median list, then the rest of the service area. Every row is a door and every door carries this page's exact population through zipSearchHref. Replaces the two KbExploreTowns grids, and drops the hardcoded '0 Active' the KB page printed beside the other nine ZIPs.

requiredComponents.name: V3PlacePropertyTypes
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 1 again, as ONE enumeration: one section per other property type this ZIP holds, from getPublicPlaceSegments, with each door carrying postalCode. A type with nothing publishable is absent, never an empty section and never a zero. Replaces PublicProductTypes.

requiredComponents.name: ZipAlertsSheet
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 5, Sheet, route-local — free listing alerts. THE CAPTURE CONTRACT IS UNCHANGED from KbCommunityAlerts: submitSearchAlertSignup with { email, filters: { city, propertyType: 'A', postalCode: zip }, company }, the same honeypot key, the same guest-watch residual and the same alert_create search event.

requiredComponents.name: ZipSellSheet
requiredComponents.section: Pattern 5, Sheet, route-local — the seller door. THE NAVIGATION CONTRACT IS UNCHANGED from KbSell: `${valuationPath()}?address=<typed>&from=<pathname>`, so the prefill survives and the lead still records which page converted. It publishes no median: the two figures KbSell printed above its form are the same numbers the market Instrument already prints under that section's own trace.

requiredComponents.name: V3Footer
requiredComponents.section: footer — rendered outside <main> so the page ships a contentinfo landmark.

removedComponents: KbHero (replaced by ZipHomesField; the count, median list and days figure are figures on the market Instrument)
KbMarketHud (replaced by V3Instrument: verdict caption, figure set, chart)
KbFeatured (replaced by ZipHomesField, which lists every active home rather than the top 14)
KbListingMap (the same Google map, in the Field's map slot, bound to the list both ways)
KbCommunityAlerts (replaced by ZipAlertsSheet, same server action and payload)
PublicPaceStats + PublicMixStats (their items are figures on the market Instrument, each carrying its own window on its label)
MarketSources (the Oregon Data Share citation is named in words inside every trace on the page)
SmoothScrollProvider (Lenis wrapper; no v3 section is scroll-bound)

The KB market HUD's question heading, 'Is ZIP {zip} a buyer's or seller's market?' — dropped by the 2026-08-26 migration pending a family decision, RESTORED the same day: Matt ruled the question stays on all five place grains. In v3 idiom it is the market Instrument's headline whenever a live verdict exists (the verdict sentence beneath it is the answer), falling back to 'Homes for sale in {zip}' when no verdict is publishable, because a question with no answer under it is worse than a label (§0). Family consistency is gated by ci:market-question (scripts/check-market-question-heading.mjs); the route's exact template is pinned in app/zip/[zip]/page.test.ts.
sectionOrder: ZipAlertsSheet (Sheet, figure beside Atlas in the opening)
V3Instrument (market, level 1) or V3Quiet when no figure is live
jsonLd: BreadcrumbList, from the same trail V3Breadcrumb renders.
Place, with the ZIP's postal address.

Dataset, with the same five variables in the same order and the same unitText: active listings, median list price, median price per sq ft, median days on market, new listings last 30 days. A degraded read publishes no variable rather than a zero.
dataLayer: getZipListings(zip, { status: 'active', propertyType: 'A', limit: 5000 }) — the Field, its map, the neighborhood Ledger, and the tile-derived Dataset variables. The 5000 cap is never reported as inventory.

getMetric({ stat, geoType: 'zip', geoSlug: zip, segment: 'detached' }) ×4 — active_count, median_list_active, months_of_supply, market_verdict. A publishable 0 that contradicts visible pins is a disagreement, not an inventory.
getPublicDetachedPace({ geoType: 'zip' }) — the leftover HUD tiles and the 12-month pace figures.
getPublicDetachedMix({ geoType: 'zip' }) — the detached mix figures.

getPublicDetachedMonthly({ geoType: 'zip' }) with the parent city's own leftover months and getPriceHistory('city', …) as the documented fallback — the median-close year overlay. When the series is the city's, the chart caption says so.
